In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of high $p_T$ hadron spectra in $Pp$, $Pb+Au$ and central $PbPb$ collisions.
the suppression of high $p_T$ hadrons in $p+p$, $d+Au$ and $Pb+Au$ collisions at RHIC and $Pb + Pb$ collisions at LHC within the NLO pQCD framework.
a quantitative understanding of suppression of large $P_{T}$ hadronic spectra in $Pp$ and $Pb+Au$ collisions in the framework of NLO perturbate QCD with medium modified fragmentation functions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the NLO pertubative QCD partonic picture of the jet quenching in the high density QCD matter is fully consistent with the ALICE data on the nuclear suppression factor $R_{Pbb}(p_{T}$ for large $p_{ T}$ hadrons.

the NLO pQCD calculations combined with the higher-twist jet quenching model and the 3 + 1D ideal hydrodynamics can simultaneously explain the RHIC data as well as the LHC data on suppression of high $p_T$ hadrons and the LHC data of charged hadron multiplicities in central $P+Pb$ and $Pb+ Pb$ collisions at the LHC.
the data are well described by a model that incorporates both jet quenching and hydrodynamic evolution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the predicted $R_{PdPb}(p_T)$ is in agreement with the preliminary data from the ALICE Collaboration at the LHC.
the suppression of large $P_{T}$ hadronic spectra in $P_{b}P_{b}$ collisions at the LHC is dominated by jet energy loss in the hot and dense medium produced in the collision.
our model calculations are in reasonable agreement with data on $R_{PpPb}(p_T)$ for neutral pions and $dN_{h}/d\eta$ for charged hadrons.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the observed strong suppression of large $ p_{T} $ hadron spectra in $PdPb$ collisions is consistent with a large initial gluon density in the medium and the effect of jet quenchings is not significant.

the large suppression of large $P_{T}$ pion spectra in central $PdPb$ collisions is consistent with the jet transport parameter determined by the RHIC $R_{AA}$ data and the initial parton densities extracted from the $dN_{Ch}/d\eta$ data at the LHC.
the observed suppression in large $p_{t}$ hadron spectra in $P+Pb$ and $Pb+ Pb$ collisions can be understood without resorting to the jet quenching scenario.
